How the numbers are built

The ladder. Each bar is the median sold price-per-acre for that lot-size band in the chosen county over the last 12 months. If a band has no closed sales it falls back to the median pending price (marked *); bands with only for-sale listings are greyed out and not used as a price. Only your parcel's band and smaller ones are shown.

Potential As-Is Value. Your acreage × the price-per-acre of the band it falls into today — the baseline every cut is measured against.

Single & mixed cut. Subdivided value is acreage × the target band's price-per-acre; in a mix, each group is priced at its own band and summed. The increase is that value over the Potential As-Is Value.

Road frontage. Total frontage ÷ parcel acreage gives feet-per-acre; each lot's frontage is then its size × that figure (so a band of 1–3 ac shows the frontage range for a 1- to 3-acre lot). It assumes frontage scales with lot size — a quick feasibility eyeball, not a survey; true frontage depends on lot shape and road layout.

Gross market figures only. Sale values, not profit — no survey, platting, road, or selling costs, and the tool doesn't know your zoning, access, or wetlands. Confirm minimum lot size, minimum road frontage, and platting exemptions before you act.
